newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico proposes deal with Europe in election spat.
newsitem.headline: Mexico proposes deal with Europe in election spat.

text.p: Mexico said on Tuesday it would allow the European Union to fund observers at this year's mid-term elections as long as funding was channeled through the United Nations.
The Mexican government last week rejected plans by the European Union to give $400,000 to the private Mexican Academy of Human Rights, saying the donation broke with protocol.

Stung by criticism that it was blocking international funding for election monitoring, Mexico's Foreign Ministry proposed that the European funding be added to a United Nations Development Program project for election monitoring.
The funds will be handled by the Federal Electoral Institute, Mexico's top electoral authority.
The key mid-term elections in July will determine who will control the lower house of Congress. Mexico City voters will also be able to vote for a mayor for the first time.
The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) has run Mexico for 68 years and has been accused of rigging past elections. Recent polls show that it could lose the Mexico City race.
